title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: Seminal paper defining IPI: attacker plants instructions in retrieved content (web/email/etc), no direct user prompt needed. Foundational technique class.
name: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI)

title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
notes: First knowledge-corruption attack targeting the RAG knowledge database itself; optimization-based crafting of malicious texts to be retrieved and induce target answer.
name: PoisonedRAG

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
notes: First backdoor/red-teaming attack poisoning agent long-term memory/RAG knowledge base via optimized trigger + few malicious demonstrations.
name: AgentPoison

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
notes: First persistent, trigger-free memory-poisoning attack exploiting agents' 'semantic imitation heuristic'; explicitly distinguished from AgentPoison/MINJA/InjecMEM.
name: MemoryGraft

title: Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents
technique_name: Sleeper Memory Poisoning (Actor-Critic universal poisoning attack)
notes: Delayed, cross-session memory poisoning attack: adversary causes assistant to write a fabricated memory that lies dormant until later retrieved; proposes Actor-Critic universal poisoning attack method.
name: Sleeper Memory Poisoning (Actor-Critic universal poisoning attack)

title: Supply-Chain Poisoning Attacks Against LLM Coding Agent Skill Ecosystems
notes: Novel software supply-chain attack surface via LLM coding agent skill ecosystems; DDIPE achieves execution bypass where explicit natural-language payloads fail (0% baseline).
name: PoisonedSkills / DDIPE (Document-Driven Implicit Payload Execution)

title: Oracle Poisoning: Corrupting Knowledge Graphs to Weaponise AI Agent Reasoning
notes: Defines and demonstrates a novel attack class corrupting structured knowledge graphs queried via MCP tool-use, causing wrong conclusions via sound reasoning over corrupted data; distinct from prompt injection and RAG poisoning.
name: Oracle Poisoning

title: Poisoning Retrieval Corpora by Injecting Adversarial Passages
technique_name: UNNAMED: gradient-based corpus poisoning (adversarial passage injection)
notes: Seminal corpus-poisoning attack on dense retrievers (Zhong et al.); crafts adversarial passages via discrete-token gradient optimization adapted from HotFlip, generalizes across queries. No proper coined name given by paper itself.
name: UNNAMED: gradient-based corpus poisoning (adversarial passage injection)

title: TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models
notes: Joint backdoor attack shifting backdoor implantation from LLM weights to the RAG knowledge-mounting component; constructs trigger sets for conditional backdoor activation.
name: TrojanRAG

title: Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
notes: Indirect jailbreak via RAG poisoning: crafts malicious documents to evade content filters and get retrieved, jailbreaking GPTs without directly prompting the target model.
name: PANDORA (RAG Poisoning jailbreak)

title: BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
notes: Conditional/triggered backdoor poisoning of RAG corpus; explicitly positioned as going beyond prior fixed query-answer poisoning (PoisonedRAG) via semantic-trigger conditioning.
name: BadRAG

title: ConfusedPilot: Confused Deputy Risks in RAG-based LLMs
notes: Names a vulnerability class (confused-deputy risk) in commercial RAG assistants (MS Copilot case study); largely qualitative demonstration rather than a novel algorithmic attack technique -- borderline between vulnerability disclosure and named attack.
name: ConfusedPilot

title: Corpus Poisoning via Approximate Greedy Gradient Descent
notes: Explicit algorithmic improvement over HotFlip's search strategy for corpus poisoning of dense retrievers; matches the 'extension of X' pattern called out in task instructions.
name: AGGD (Approximate Greedy Gradient Descent)

title: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
notes: First generic black-box automated red-teaming framework for IPI vulnerabilities, adapting fuzzing to multi-step agent setting; works without white-box access unlike prior automated attacks (AgentPoison, VWA-adv).
name: AgentVigil

title: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
technique_name: UNNAMED: HTML accessibility-tree universal adversarial trigger injection (TWUI)
notes: Adapts GCG to IPI setting for web agents by embedding universal adversarial triggers in webpage HTML/accessibility tree with flexible (non-suffix) trigger placement and an extended objective; meaningful adaptation but core search algorithm is GCG, so borderline extension vs application.
name: UNNAMED: HTML accessibility-tree universal adversarial trigger injection (TWUI)

title: AGENTFUZZER: Generic Black-Box Fuzzing for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
technique_name: UNNAMED: AgentFuzzer (generic black-box fuzzing for IPI)
notes: Source Excel row had empty abstract/technical_summary/key_result fields -- judgment based on title alone ('Generic Black-Box Fuzzing for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents'). Appears to propose a fuzzing-based automated attack-generation technique distinct in name from AgentVigil, but cannot confirm novelty/algorithm details from available data. Needs manual follow-up.
name: UNNAMED: AgentFuzzer (generic black-box fuzzing for IPI)

title: AdapTools: Adaptive Tool-based Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic LLMs
notes: Adaptive tool-based IPI attack designed to defeat reasoning-capable agents that cross-verify tool calls via CoT; identifies 'trinity of constraints' (adaptability, etc.) and proposes attacks satisfying them, addressing a gap where prior static template-based IPI attacks fail against reasoning models.
name: AdapTools

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
notes: Formalizes IPI attacks that must actually be retrieved under natural queries (unlike prior work assuming pre-retrieved malicious text); decomposes malicious content into a retrieval-trigger fragment plus payload to jointly satisfy retrievability and injection, closing the 'retrieval barrier' gap.
name: UNNAMED: retrieval-aware IPI (trigger-fragment decomposition attack)

title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: Fully automated multi-agent red-teaming framework discovering IPI attacks against web agents end-to-end in sandboxed cross-app environment; automatically identifies/ranks vulnerable injection surfaces, novel attack-discovery methodology vs prior manual/template-based approaches.
name: MUZZLE

title: IterInject: Indirect Prompt Injection Against LLM Agents via Feedback-Guided Iterative Optimization
notes: Feedback-guided iterative optimization framework for IPI attacks that closes the loop between injection, diagnosis, and refinement, addressing limitations of static handcrafted payloads and unstructured adaptive methods.
name: IterInject

title: LogJack: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Cloud Logs Against LLM Debugging Agents
notes: Studies a previously unevaluated IPI attack surface: cloud telemetry/log data (CloudWatch, SSM, CloudTrail, CI/CD, Lambda logs) consumed by LLM cloud-debugging agents; attacker embeds payload in application error text without special cloud privileges.
name: LogJack

title: ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
notes: Exploits LLM agents' structural dependence on chat templates (role tokens enforcing system>user>assistant>tool priority) by formatting a malicious tool-response payload to mimic higher-priority roles, combined with persuasive multi-turn framing; a previously underexplored injection vulnerability.
name: ChatInject

title: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
technique_name: UNNAMED: in-browser LLM-guided fuzzing for agentic-browser IPI
notes: Novel fuzzing framework operating entirely within a live browser context (isolated tab, full DOM/rendering/script execution) rather than offline text simulation, preserving CSS-hiding, dynamic JS DOM modification, timing side-channel, and browser-API attack vectors invisible to prior offline approaches. No proper name coined by the paper.
name: UNNAMED: in-browser LLM-guided fuzzing for agentic-browser IPI

title: Whispers of Wealth: Red-Teaming Google's Agent Payments Protocol via Prompt Injection
technique_name: Branded Whisper Attack / Vault Whisper Attack (from 'Whispers of Wealth')
notes: Two novel reasoning-layer attack techniques against Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2): Branded Whisper (indirect prompt injection via malicious merchant product metadata biasing ranking) and Vault Whisper (direct prompt injection attempting to override identity-based access constraints during credential retrieval). Exploits that AP2 secures execution correctness but not reasoning integrity.
name: Branded Whisper Attack / Vault Whisper Attack (from 'Whispers of Wealth')

title: An Empirical Study of Privacy Leakage Chains via Prompt Injection in Black-Box Chatbot Environments
technique_name: UNNAMED: privacy leakage attack chain (external-content deception + IPI + exfiltration)
notes: Demonstrates a multi-stage attack chain end-to-end against deployed black-box ChatGPT combining external-content deception (e.g. CSS-hidden instructions), indirect prompt injection, and data exfiltration; a systematization/combination of known primitives into a proven real-world chain rather than a single novel algorithmic technique -- borderline, similar to ConfusedPilot (row 21).
name: UNNAMED: privacy leakage attack chain (external-content deception + IPI + exfiltration)

title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
technique_name: MIRAGE (Masked Injection via Residual And Generative Exploitation)
notes: Stealthy visual indirect-prompt-injection attack against screenshot-based MLLM web agents; attacker confined to a spatially bounded legitimate visual region (e.g. ad slot), cannot touch DOM/UI/prompt, must avoid visible artifacts -- a novel restrictive threat model and technique.
name: MIRAGE (Masked Injection via Residual And Generative Exploitation)

title: Document-Authored Control-Signal Impersonation: A Low-Cost Indirect Prompt Attack on RAG Safety Boundaries
notes: Defines a new IPI payload subclass distinguished from command-style injection: payloads contain no imperative language, instead impersonating metadata/provenance/authority/disclosure-policy signals embedded in retrievable documents to manipulate RAG safety boundaries.
name: DACSI (Document-Authored Control-Signal Impersonation)

title: PI-Hunter: Automated Red-Teaming for Exposing and Localizing Prompt Injections
notes: Automated agentic security-auditing/red-teaming framework that reframes IPI red-teaming from attack-success optimization toward proactive vulnerability exposure -- systematically mapping an agent's full security perimeter to flush out hidden/dormant injections, distinct methodology from prior automated red-teamers (SafeSearch, GOAT, AutoRedTeamer, SIRAJ).
name: PI-Hunter

title: Invisible Threats from Model Context Protocol: Generating Stealthy Injection Payload via Tree-based Adaptive Search
technique_name: TIP (Tree-structured Injection for Payloads) / stealthy update attack
notes: Black-box adversarial attack framework generating stealthy injection payloads against MCP servers via tree-based adaptive search; formalizes a novel 'stealthy update attack' vulnerability where a malicious/compromised MCP server injects adversarial payloads into response fields post-approval.
name: TIP (Tree-structured Injection for Payloads) / stealthy update attack

title: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
notes: New IPI attack category mechanistically distinct from and orthogonal to 'instruction injection': causes untrusted data to be misinterpreted as trusted data (rather than as an instruction to follow), exploiting agents' failure to isolate trust levels of data sources.
name: Agent Data Injection (ADI)

title: VATS: Exploiting Implicit Authority in Error-Path Injection via Systematic Mutation
notes: Isolates and exploits the MCP tool-calling error-handling loop as a distinct attack surface from general tool-output IPI; hypothesizes/demonstrates that error messages carry 'implicit authority' activating corrective reasoning that bypasses normal skepticism heuristics.
name: VATS (Error-Path Injection via Implicit Authority)

title: Invitation Is All You Need! Promptware Attacks Against LLM-Powered Assistants in Production Are Practical and Dangerous
notes: Empirical, responsibly-disclosed red-team study against real production Gemini-powered assistants (Web/Mobile/Google Assistant); introduces Targeted Promptware Attacks, a variant of indirect prompt injection, showing attacks are practical without adversarial-ML expertise or white-box access.
name: Targeted Promptware Attacks

title: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage
technique_name: OMNI-LEAK (Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage)
notes: Novel attack vector showing a single IPI can compromise multiple agents within the orchestrator multi-agent pattern to coordinate data exfiltration, even when individual agents are protected by data access controls; payload embedded in attacker-writable public data.
name: OMNI-LEAK (Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage)

title: Breaking ReAct Agents: Foot-in-the-Door Attack Will Get You In
notes: Novel enhancement to IPI against ReAct agents inspired by psychological compliance ('foot-in-the-door') phenomenon: prepends a small harmless distractor request before the malicious payload to increase compliance, built on InjecAgent's IPI attack corpus.
name: Foot-in-the-Door (FITD) attack

title: Taxonomy, Evaluation and Exploitation of IPI-Centric LLM Agent Defense Frameworks
technique_name: Semantic-Masquerading IPI; Cascading IPI; Isolation-Breach IPI
notes: SoK paper on IPI-centric defenses that ALSO designs and demonstrates three novel logic-driven (non-gradient) adaptive attacks, each targeting a specific defense-failure root cause identified in the paper's taxonomy: Semantic-Masquerading IPI (adapts payloads to functionally-similar tools evading access control), Cascading IPI (head/body/end if-then-else payload structure targeting auxiliary judge-LLM defenses like Task Shield/MELON), and Isolation-Breach IPI (exploits error-message/feedback channels to inject into architecturally 'trusted' planner components, bypassing IsolateGPT).
name: Semantic-Masquerading IPI; Cascading IPI; Isolation-Breach IPI

title: Bypassing AI Control Protocols via Agent-as-a-Proxy Attacks
notes: Demonstrates that SOTA hybrid monitoring-based defenses (jointly scrutinizing agent CoT reasoning + tool-call actions, e.g. AlignmentCheck, LlamaFirewall) can be systematically bypassed, challenging the assumption that reasoning+action visibility gives stronger defense than input-only observation.
name: Agent-as-a-Proxy attack

title: Confused ChatGPT: Cross-App Context Poisoning via First-Party APIs
notes: First systematic security analysis of OpenAI's ChatGPT Apps platform ('app-in-app' ecosystem sharing a flat untagged chat context across all connected apps); reverse-engineers client-side JS to identify channels by which one app's content can poison context shared with other apps/the user.
name: Cross-App Context Poisoning (Confused ChatGPT)

title: AutoDojo: Adaptive Black-Box Attacks Reveal the Limits of IPI Defenses and Task-Specification Effects in LLM Agents
notes: Argues published IPI defenses' strong reported protection is partly an artifact of testing only against fixed hand-written injection strings from static benchmarks (AgentDojo); introduces AutoDojo, an adaptive black-box attack-generation approach to reveal true defense limits and task-specification effects.
name: AutoDojo (adaptive black-box IPI attack generation)

title: Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents
notes: First prompt injection attack specifically targeting the tool-selection process of LLM agents in a realistic no-box setting (attacker only publishes a malicious tool document to an open third-party tool platform, no access to task descriptions/retriever/LLM/tool library).
name: ToolHijacker

title: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
notes: Prompt injection attack targeting screenshot-perceiving MLLM web agents; perturbs the webpage's underlying raw pixel values via source-code modification (rather than visible HTML or direct screenshot perturbation) so the rendered screenshot carries the adversarial payload.
name: WebInject

title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
notes: Cross-modal prompt injection attack framework for black-box multimodal agents, coordinating Visual Latent Alignment (text-to-image synthesis semantically aligned in latent space) with complementary components to exploit cross-modal fusion, unlike prior single-modality attacks.
name: CrossInject

title: RL Is a Hammer and LLMs Are Nails: A Simple Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Strong Prompt Injection
notes: Reinforcement-learning recipe (GRPO fine-tuning of an attacker LLM from scratch, no warm-up/curated dataset) training a black-box automated red-teaming attacker that generates strong universal prompt injection/jailbreak attacks defeating SOTA defenses (Instruction Hierarchy, SecAlign).
name: RL-Hammer

title: Prompt Injection 2.0: Hybrid AI Threats
technique_name: UNNAMED: Prompt Injection 2.0 (hybrid PI + classic web-exploit combination attacks)
notes: Industry whitepaper tracing evolution of PI to hybrid threats combining prompt injection with XSS/CSRF/SQL injection to evade both AI-specific and conventional web defenses; names a new threat category ('Prompt Injection 2.0') but is framed as an industry analysis/taxonomy rather than a single peer-reviewed algorithmic technique -- flagged low confidence.
name: UNNAMED: Prompt Injection 2.0 (hybrid PI + classic web-exploit combination attacks)

title: Simple Prompt Injection Attacks Can Leak Personal Data Observed by LLM Agents During Task Execution
technique_name: UNNAMED: data flow-based injection attack for observed-data exfiltration ('Important message' template)
notes: Extends AgentDojo's banking suite to study exfiltration of personal data an agent merely observes during normal task execution (not just data pulled from attacker-controlled external tools); crafts an 'Important message' template attack impersonating the user. Borderline -- a meaningful new threat variant built on AgentDojo's existing tasks/injection style rather than a fully new algorithm.
name: UNNAMED: data flow-based injection attack for observed-data exfiltration ('Important message' template)

title: ObliInjection: Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data
notes: First prompt injection attack designed for multi-source input assembly settings, where the attacker controls only a subset of sources and does not know the final concatenation order ('order-oblivious').
name: ObliInjection

title: Fun-tuning: Characterizing the Vulnerability of Proprietary LLMs to Optimization-Based Prompt Injection Attacks via the Fine-Tuning Interface
notes: New graybox attack vector against closed-weight commercial LLMs that misuses the vendor's legitimate remote fine-tuning API (e.g. Gemini Fine-Tuning API) as a loss-value oracle to compute optimization-based indirect prompt injection attacks, despite no logprob/gradient access via the normal inference endpoint.
name: Fun-tuning

title: "Your AI, My Shell": Demystifying Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic AI Coding Editors
technique_name: AIShellJack (coding-rule/config-file prompt injection against agentic IDE editors)
notes: First systematic empirical study of PI against agentic AI coding editors (Cursor, GitHub Copilot); exploits that developers import untrusted coding-rule/config files, forked repos, and MCP server configs into IDE workspaces without security vetting, turning the editor into an attacker's shell; builds AIShellJack automated evaluation framework with a payload-construction pipeline.
name: AIShellJack (coding-rule/config-file prompt injection against agentic IDE editors)

title: Prompt Injection attack against LLM-integrated Applications
notes: First systematic black-box methodology for PI against real-world commercial LLM-integrated applications; three-phase attack toolkit (context inference via auxiliary LLM observing input-output behavior, three-part payload generation with novel Separator Component, and iterative refinement), explicitly analogized to classical SQL injection/XSS, more powerful than prior ad hoc 'ignore previous context' heuristics.
name: HOUYI

title: Mind Mapping Prompt Injection: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks in Modern Large Language Models
notes: Visual prompt injection technique named directly in the title/abstract; source Excel row had an empty technical_summary field so algorithmic details are limited, but the paper clearly coins and studies this specific named technique.
name: Mind Mapping Prompt Injection

title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: Reframes construction of PI 'execution triggers' (prefix+suffix wrapper forcing an LLM to treat an injected payload as an instruction) as a differentiable, GCG-style discrete optimization problem rather than manual prompt engineering, with teacher-forced log-likelihood and positional decay weighting.
name: Neural Exec

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-agent Systems
notes: Foundational paper revealing that IPI in multi-agent LLM systems can self-replicate across interconnected agents like a computer virus, propagating malicious instructions agent-to-agent through normal communication channels rather than compromising just one agent.
name: Prompt Infection

title: Cybersecurity AI: Hacking the AI Hackers via Prompt Injection
technique_name: UNNAMED: PI-based counter-attack on offensive AI cybersecurity agents (four-stage attack anatomy + seven-category taxonomy incl. Unicode homograph exploitation)
notes: Demonstrates that AI-powered offensive pentesting agents (e.g. Cybersecurity AI/CAI framework) can be compromised via PI delivered through content they analyze; documents a four-stage attack anatomy and a seven-category attack taxonomy including 'previously undocumented techniques' per the paper (e.g. Unicode homograph exploitation); shows explicit data/instruction separation guardrails can paradoxically increase attack success.
name: UNNAMED: PI-based counter-attack on offensive AI cybersecurity agents (four-stage attack anatomy + seven-category taxonomy incl. Unicode homograph exploitation)

title: System Prompt Poisoning: Persistent Attacks on Large Language Models Beyond User Injection
notes: Introduces and formally defines a new LLM attack vector distinct from user-prompt injection: corrupts the system prompt itself for persistent, wide-ranging compromise affecting every subsequent user interaction regardless of query.
name: System Prompt Poisoning (SPP)

title: Breaking the Prompt Wall (I): A Real-World Case Study of Attacking ChatGPT via Lightweight Prompt Injection
technique_name: UNNAMED: rule-tag semantic reframing template attack ('Breaking the Prompt Wall')
notes: Real-world case study (not systematic evaluation) proposing a template-based prompting strategy that reframes harmful goals as benign-looking rule sets (e.g. <rule> tags) for semantic stealthiness and cross-model transferability, demonstrated via three real-world ChatGPT/GPTs injection vectors; borderline since the paper itself cites prior work on near-universal single-template attacks, so novelty of the core template mechanism vs. application is unclear.
name: UNNAMED: rule-tag semantic reframing template attack ('Breaking the Prompt Wall')

title: AgentTypo: Adaptive Typographic Prompt Injection Attacks against Black-box Multimodal Agents
notes: Black-box red-teaming framework performing adaptive typographic PI against multimodal (LVLM) web agents by embedding optimized adversarial text directly into webpage images, distinct from raw-HTML text injection and from CLIP-based adversarial image perturbations.
name: AgentTypo

title: MAD-Spear: A Conformity-Driven Prompt Injection Attack on Multi-Agent Debate Systems
notes: Targeted PI attack against multi-agent debate (MAD) systems; compromises only a small subset of agents via injection, drawing on Sybil-attack concepts from distributed systems to make compromised agents impersonate/manufacture apparent majority consensus.
name: MAD-Spear (Conformity-Driven Prompt Injection Attack)

title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud
technique_name: Indirect Data Poisoning (Distributed Denial of Science)
notes: Introduces and empirically validates a novel attack in which a remote adversary weaponizes honest use of autonomous AI research agents to industrialize scientific fraud at scale, modeled on historical corporate scientific-fraud campaigns; requires only an open, loosely-moderated data ecosystem plus a few other preconditions.
name: Indirect Data Poisoning (Distributed Denial of Science)

title: VeriGrey: Greybox Agent Validation
notes: Adapts grey-box software fuzzing methodology to systematically test LLM agents for security vulnerabilities (particularly IPI), using observed tool-invocation sequences as a grey-box feedback function analogous to code coverage -- a meaningful novel adaptation of an existing methodology to a new attack-discovery domain.
name: VeriGrey (grey-box agent fuzzing for IPI)

title: A Whole New World: Creating a Parallel-Poisoned Web Only AI-Agents Can See
technique_name: Parallel-Poisoned Web (fingerprinting + website cloaking against AI web agents)
notes: Novel attack vector combining browser/device fingerprinting with website cloaking (previously used for black-hat SEO/phishing) repurposed to detect and selectively serve poisoned content only to autonomous web-browsing LLM agents, exploiting agents' unusually homogeneous digital fingerprints relative to human browsers.
name: Parallel-Poisoned Web (fingerprinting + website cloaking against AI web agents)

title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code
notes: New class of control-flow hijacking attacks against LLM-based multi-agent systems, distinct from jailbreaking/IPI/prompt infection; exploits that MAS orchestrators blindly trust status/error metadata reported by sub-agents that processed adversarial content, a confused-deputy-style vulnerability.
name: MAS hijacking

title: MCP-ITP: An Automated Framework for Implicit Tool Poisoning in MCP
notes: First automated, adaptive black-box framework for 'implicit tool poisoning' attacks against MCP agents -- a stealthier variant where the poisoned tool is never directly invoked; instead its registered metadata description is crafted purely to manipulate agent behavior toward other legitimate tools.
name: MCP-ITP (Implicit Tool Poisoning)

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Protecting LLM Agents Against Tool Description Poisoning via Isolated Planning
notes: Formalizes a new attack in which an adversary manipulates a non-critical tool's description metadata to steer an agent's planner into maliciously invoking a different, safety-critical tool, without the poisoned tool ever being selected itself; paper's headline contribution is the Isolated Planning defense, but the attack is explicitly formalized/named as its own concept -- similar dual attack+defense pattern to BadRAG.
name: Cross-Tool Description Poisoning

title: Semantic Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLMs: Securing the Model Context Protocol Against Descriptor-Level Manipulation
technique_name: UNNAMED: descriptor-level semantic manipulation attack (MCP tool-selection bias)
notes: Identifies and formalizes a previously underexplored MCP-specific semantic attack surface: subtle wording manipulations in natural-language tool descriptors bias agent tool selection/interpretation independent of user input, schema validity, or code compromise; paper title emphasizes 'Securing MCP' so defense may be co-equal contribution -- flagged low confidence on whether attack or defense is the primary novel contribution.
name: UNNAMED: descriptor-level semantic manipulation attack (MCP tool-selection bias)

title: Automatic Red Teaming LLM-Based Agents With Model Context Protocol Tools
notes: First automated red-teaming framework for systematically generating malicious MCP tools (tool poisoning via metadata rather than executable code), analogous in kind to AgentVigil/MUZZLE-style automated attack-discovery frameworks but targeting MCP tool generation specifically.
name: AutoMalTool

title: Parasites in the Toolchain: A Large-Scale Analysis of Attacks on the MCP Ecosystem
technique_name: Parasitic Toolchain Attacks (MCP Unintended Privacy Disclosure, MCP-UPD)
notes: New class of privacy-leakage attacks against the MCP ecosystem exploiting composition of multiple independently benign, legitimate MCP tools/servers into an emergent malicious workflow, unlike prior work limited to a single compromised server.
name: Parasitic Toolchain Attacks (MCP Unintended Privacy Disclosure, MCP-UPD)

title: Salience Induction against Multi-Hop RAG Agents: Threat and Defense
notes: Novel, truth-preserving attack surface against agentic multi-hop RAG systems, orthogonal to content poisoning (false facts) and prompt injection (imperative directives): manipulates how factually correct object-value bindings are resolved from free-form textual cues at each reasoning hop.
name: Salience Induction

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
is_extension_of: PoisonedRAG (adds prompt-injection component to corpus poisoning)
notes: Compound, query-agnostic attack on RAG combining prompt injection (query-path manipulation) with database/corpus poisoning (corpus-path manipulation) in one adversarial suffix, unlike prior poisoning attacks (e.g. PoisonedRAG) that require knowing the target query in advance.
name: PIDP-Attack

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
notes: Two-stage word-level RAG poisoning (Macro Generation + Micro Refinement) explicitly positioned as stealthier successor to PoisonedRAG's separate-and-concatenate strategy
name: RefineRAG

title: Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
notes: Novel backdoor attack targeting dense-retriever fine-tuning (distinct from the paper's baseline PoisonedRAG-style corpus poisoning); paper explicitly calls it 'a novel backdoor attack' but gives it no proper name
name: UNNAMED: retriever fine-tuning backdoor attack

title: When Compression Becomes an Attack Surface: Black-Box Attacks on Prompt-Compressed LLM Agents
notes: Novel attack surface: black-box perturbation of untrusted input to corrupt shared-budget prompt compression before inference, explicitly distinguished from prompt injection/jailbreaks/RAG poisoning
name: COMA

title: LogicPoison: Logical Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Novel structural/topological attack on GraphRAG knowledge graphs, distinct mechanism from text-based RAG poisoning (bypasses GraphRAG's synthetic-entity filtering)
name: LogicPoison

title: Silent Leaks: Implicit Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems through Benign Queries
notes: Novel stealthy knowledge-extraction attack using benign queries + anchor concepts, explicitly first of its kind vs prior malicious-input extraction attacks (RAG-Thief, DGEA)
name: IKEA (Implicit Knowledge Extraction Attack)

title: FlashRT: Towards Computationally and Memory Efficient Red-Teaming for Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
notes: Efficient optimization-based red-teaming algorithm for prompt injection/knowledge corruption matching SOTA ASR at 2-7x speedup and 2-4x lower memory vs nanoGCG; algorithmic improvement over gradient-based search methods
name: FlashRT

title: From Untrusted Input to Trusted Memory: A Systematic Study of Memory Poisoning Attacks in LLM Agents
technique_name: UNNAMED: memory-poisoning attack taxonomy (6 classes incl. Conditional Command Insertion, Policy-Conformant Fact Injection, False Precedent Insertion)
notes: Introduces a taxonomy of 6 novel memory-poisoning attack classes plus MPBench benchmark; borderline between systematic-study/taxonomy paper (exclude) and set of genuinely new attack techniques (include) -- worth spot-check for whether dedup should register individual attack classes
name: UNNAMED: memory-poisoning attack taxonomy (6 classes incl. Conditional Command Insertion, Policy-Conformant Fact Injection, False Precedent Insertion)

title: The Dark Side of LLMs: Agent-based Attack Vectors for System-level Compromise
technique_name: Inter-Agent Trust Exploitation (AI agent privilege escalation)
notes: Novel attack surface exploiting asymmetric trust between AI-AI vs human-AI interaction in multi-agent systems, achieving 100% success even against models resistant to direct injection/RAG backdoor; explicitly named phenomenon 'AI agent privilege escalation'
name: Inter-Agent Trust Exploitation (AI agent privilege escalation)

title: Security Risk Evaluation of ZombAI Claude: Prompt Injection as a Backdoor for Command and Control Exploits
notes: Named black-box attack method with six distinct strategies (Template Completion, In-Context Attack, Code Injection, Prompt Rewriting, etc.) targeting Claude Computer Use for C2 exploitation
name: ZombAI

title: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
mechanism_name: mechanistic explanation of knowledge conflict via information-flow/attention-head circuit (PH3)
notes: Mechanistic-interpretability paper explaining knowledge-conflict resolution via a specific causal circuit; borderline new-entry vs. refinement of existing "knowledge conflict" per prompt guidance on mechanistic explanations.
name: mechanistic explanation of knowledge conflict via information-flow/attention-head circuit (PH3)

title: Tug-of-War between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
mechanism_name: UNNAMED: over-trust bias toward conflicting external evidence over correct parametric memory in RALMs
notes: Exploratory finding that RALMs readily abandon correct internal beliefs in favor of conflicting retrieved evidence; a specific characterized behavioral bias within knowledge-conflict literature, not given its own name by authors.
name: UNNAMED: over-trust bias toward conflicting external evidence over correct parametric memory in RALMs

title: State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
notes: Central, novel finding: toxic/adversarial context compressed into memory summaries by multi-agent systems evades standard toxicity classifiers while preserving hostile framing/conflict signal. Paper explicitly frames this as a non-adversarial-injection incidental failure mode of routine summarization.
name: memory laundering

title: MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Memory MisEvolution in LLM Agents
notes: Benchmark paper explicitly naming and characterizing "memory misevolution": gradual, self-reinforcing behavioral drift from repeated exposure to misleading information accumulated in persistent memory, distinguished by the authors from prior one-shot poisoning/static hallucination framings.
name: memory misevolution

title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents
notes: Central, explicitly formalized and named contribution: progressive erosion of an autonomous agent's adherence to an explicit behavioral mandate as context accumulates over a long deployment horizon, even while individual decisions remain locally coherent.
name: Mandate Salience Decay (MSD)

title: Context-Aware RL for Agentic and Multimodal LLMs
mechanism_name: context unawareness (failure to identify a small decisive piece of evidence within long/complex context)
notes: Names the failure mode motivating an auxiliary RL objective; overlaps substantially with existing needle-in-a-haystack/distraction framings.
name: context unawareness (failure to identify a small decisive piece of evidence within long/complex context)

title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
notes: Paper coins "Contextual Belief Management" and measurable sub-failures (Failed Stay/Update/Isolation Rate) for inappropriate belief updates under accumulating long-horizon context; primarily a benchmark/framework, borderline whether distinct enough from knowledge-conflict/ToM framings.
name: Contextual Belief Management (CBM) failure

title: Episodic-Semantic Memory Architecture for Long-Horizon Scientific Agents
mechanism_name: UNNAMED: "cognitive event horizon" (context-saturation threshold beyond which accuracy collapses)
notes: Paper identifies a discontinuous accuracy-collapse threshold as scientific-agent context saturates (e.g., Full-Context crashing to 0% accuracy at 10,000+ messages); term used descriptively by authors but not deeply formalized as a general phenomenon.
name: UNNAMED: "cognitive event horizon" (context-saturation threshold beyond which accuracy collapses)

title: VideoSEAL: Mitigating Evidence Misalignment in Agentic Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Answer Authority
notes: Central named contribution: agentic long-video-QA systems produce correct-looking answers not actually grounded in the evidence they retrieved/inspected; paper introduces diagnostics (temporal/semantic groundedness) to characterize it.
name: evidence misalignment (agentic long-video QA)

title: TACT: Mitigating Overthinking and Overacting in Coding Agents via Activation Steering
notes: Central named contribution: degradation over long agentic coding trajectories manifesting as two characterized sub-modes -- overthinking (redundant re-reasoning over already-known info) and overacting (issuing tool calls without integrating recent observations).
name: agent drift (overthinking / overacting)

title: Structurally Aligned Subtask-Level Memory for Software Engineering Agents
mechanism_name: UNNAMED: granularity mismatch in agent memory retrieval (instance-level memory causing both irrelevant-guidance retrieval and missed cross-task reuse)
notes: Central empirical diagnosis: coarse instance-level (whole-episode) memory indexing in SWE agents causes surface-similar issues to retrieve misleading guidance and surface-dissimilar-but-logically-similar issues to miss applicable guidance.
name: UNNAMED: granularity mismatch in agent memory retrieval (instance-level memory causing both irrelevant-guidance retrieval and missed cross-task reuse)

title: CodeDelegator: Mitigating Context Pollution via Role Separation in Code-as-Action Agents
mechanism_name: context pollution (role conflation in single-agent code-as-action agents)
notes: Paper explicitly uses the term "context pollution" for a specific mechanism: using one agent for both planning and implementation causes debugging traces/intermediate failures to dilute task-relevant information over long horizons. Term is generic/overlaps with the survey's own umbrella vocabulary; flagged for dedup-stage judgment.
name: context pollution (role conflation in single-agent code-as-action agents)

title: Rhea: Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs
mechanism_name: cumulative contextual decay (attention pollution, dilution, and drift)
notes: Central, explicitly defined contribution: progressive degradation of contextual integrity in multi-turn LLM conversation, decomposed into three named interacting sub-mechanisms (attention pollution, dilution, drift).
name: cumulative contextual decay (attention pollution, dilution, and drift)

title: Alleviating Contextual Misguidance: Response-Aware Prompt Compression for Long-Context Question Answering
notes: Paper identifies a specific causal mechanism underlying "Lost in the Middle": query-relevant yet non-grounding/misleading spans in long context misdirect the model, distinct from mere positional forgetting -- a mechanistic refinement of the established phenomenon.
name: contextual misguidance

title: Taming Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
mechanism_name: superposition of contextual information and parametric memory (mechanistic explanation of knowledge conflict)
notes: Mechanistic-interpretability finding overturning the prior "exclusive memory heads vs. context heads" assumption: influential attention heads simultaneously encode both parametric and contextual signals. A mechanistic refinement of the established knowledge-conflict phenomenon.
name: superposition of contextual information and parametric memory (mechanistic explanation of knowledge conflict)

title: Periodic RoPE for Infinite Context LLMs
is_extension_of: lost in the middle / long-context positional degradation
notes: Paper names and characterizes "position exhaustion": perplexity spikes and generation quality degrades once sequence length exceeds the positional-encoding range seen during training, distinct from (but related to) general long-context degradation.
name: position exhaustion

title: Free(): Learning to Forget in Malloc-Only Reasoning Models
mechanism_name: UNNAMED: "malloc-only" context accumulation causing reasoning degeneration in extended CoT
notes: Paper diagnoses standard reasoning LLMs as "malloc-only" engines that continuously accumulate valid and redundant reasoning steps without a pruning mechanism, causing degeneration/repetitive loops and eventual reasoning collapse past a token threshold; a specific characterized architectural failure, though "malloc-only" is more a metaphor/label than an established term.
name: UNNAMED: "malloc-only" context accumulation causing reasoning degeneration in extended CoT

title: Mitigating Scaffolding Collapse in Socratic Tutors via Representation Alignment
notes: Central named contribution: under sustained multi-turn student pressure (persistent requests, fake mastery claims, emotional urgency, role redefinition), an LLM Socratic tutor gradually abandons guided-inquiry constraints and reveals answers directly, driven by internal representation drift. Note: threat model is framed as red-teaming/sustained user pressure, bordering on Track A; included here as the paper frames it as incidental multi-turn dialogue drift rather than a discrete attack.
name: scaffolding collapse

title: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
notes: Paper names and characterizes a specific failure of activation/persona-vector steering in stateful multi-turn dialogue: steered token states are persisted and reused via the KV cache, turning a local single-turn perturbation into cumulative coherence degradation across turns.
name: KV-cache contamination

title: Unraveling Cross-Modality Knowledge Conflicts in Large Vision-Language Models
notes: Formally defines and systematically studies a new named sub-type of knowledge conflict specific to vision-language models: inconsistency between knowledge encoded in the vision pathway vs. the language backbone, causing contradictory answers depending on modality of presentation.
name: cross-modality parametric knowledge conflict
